correctness.rationale: Every nonzero square-zero 3x3 matrix has rank one; rank-one target sums admit a complete common-row/common-column inclusion-exclusion, and rank-two sums correspond bijectively to rank-one idempotents P on the target image satisfying tr(PM)=0. Counting projectors by rational eigenlines gives every fiber over all fields. Characteristic-dependent similarity strata and centralizer calculations give target populations; weighted fiber mass equals (q^4+q^3−q)^2. Direct exhaustive tests at q=2,3,4 and additional supported/sampled q=5 cases corroborate the argument, but are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed novel content is the exact positive representation count for every prescribed size-three target and the accompanying class populations. The stronger known all-size existence/support criteria of Botha and de Seguins Pazzis are explicitly acknowledged. Searches directed at additive convolution, similarity, rank-one nilpotent sums, and characteristic-two multiplicities did not locate a prior count formula; priority is provisional given inaccessible source texts.
residual_risks: The original 2012 Botha paper and 2013 Song–Zheng–Cao article were not inspected in full; an unlocated result within them may include multiplicities.
A general theorem for the additive convolution of rank-one nilpotent matrices or an equivalent association-scheme calculation might subsume the exact formula.
Search failure cannot prove historical uniqueness or independent priority.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural complete prescribed-output invariant of two square-zero summands in the first matrix dimension where rank-two sums and nontrivial characteristic-two obstructions occur. It discriminates split, nonsplit, Jordan, and regular-nilpotent targets by exact counts, supplies exact representable-target populations and an independent all-q proof. It quantifies witness multiplicity beyond the known zero/nonzero classification; no downstream theorem is required for this naturally defined census.
